topic: How do GEO vs LEO satellite orbits affect latency and coverage in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring?
consensus_response: GEO satellites have large footprints, leading to increased co-channel interference and reduced coverage probability in rural areas. In contrast, LEO orbits offer lower delay and pointing requirements but require more complex signal processing. The integration of satellite networks with terrestrial infrastructure can address issues related to latency, capacity, and reliability in rural areas. However, this requires careful optimization of the satellite constellation and ground infrastructure to ensure reliable communication.
reference_context: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) mega constellations provide global coverage with reduced propagation delays, making them suitable for applications requiring fast data transmission, such as massive machine type communications (MTC) and enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB).
